name: áes dána

attributes.attribute: Old Irish term that today names celebrated artists in Ireland
derived from the Old Irish word for poets
also applied to druids, brehons, and lawyers
gave the gift of inspiration to those who drank from it
its flesh passed on inspiration to those who tasted it
professional class of poets and craftsmen in Old Irish law

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Áes dána is the Old Irish term for the people of art or of a craft trade, and especially for poets. The phrase carries the sense of a professional class whose skill defines them, distinct from the warrior or the field-labourer. In early Irish literature the áes dána names a social category whose privileges and obligations the law tracts record. A modern Irish form, dána, survives as a related word.

okr.objective: Define áes dána as the Old Irish term for the people of art, especially poets.
key_results: Anchor the Old Irish etymology people of art.
Place the term within the social categories of early Irish law.

objective: To explain the meaning and origin of the Irish phrase áes dána.
key_results: In modern Ireland the phrase means a group of nationally acclaimed artists.
It derives from the Old Irish term for poets.
It was also applied to Druids, Brehons, or lawyers.
Inspiration came from the Well of wisdom, its hazel nuts, or the salmon that swam in it.
In Old Irish the áes dána were the learned classes who shaped the common literary language.
evidence: The phrase áes dána derives from the Old Irish term for poets and was also applied to Druids, Brehons, or lawyers.
